newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia bond yields lower, restrained by US jobs.
newsitem.headline: Australia bond yields lower, restrained by US jobs.

text.p: *Australian bond yields were lower following comments by RBA governor Macfarlane in London which seen leaving the way open for a further easing in monetary policy.
*Trade expected to be light ahead of holiday, U.S. payrolls.
Australian bond yields were lower following comments by Reserve Bank governor Ian Macfarlane in London which seen leaving the way open for a further easing.

Macfarlane said Australia had considerable spare capacity in the economy, and while he expected a pick-up in growth in 1997/98, the central bank was aiming for a sustained period of low inflation growth.

"Some people are looking the excess capacity part of the speech and think he has left the window open for an easing, but I don't think they will," said Stephen Roberts, chief economist at UBS Australia.
"I would be looking for them (the RBA) needing to see at least the May quarter average weekly earnings before they can make a decision on monetary policy," Roberts added.

Macfarlane told a bank seminar in London that last month's wages data had pushed the central bank in to its May 23 easing to 5.5 percent. The next wages data are not due until mid-August and by that time the economy could already be showing signs of a strong recovery, economists said.
However, while rate cut speculation continued to underpin the market, turnover was fairly light ahead of the long holiday weekend and the U.S. non-farm payrolls data laqter on Friday.
The market's firm tone saw it outperform the dollar bloc and the yield curve steepen slightly.
U.S. Treasuries ended little changed on Thursday ahead of the May labour forece data.
Payrolls are forecast to rise 221,000 after the 142,000 increase in April.
